discoveries.headline: Stablecoins in five minutes, from the Bank of England
discoveries.why: A central bank's plain answer to the crypto everyone actually uses: what backs a stablecoin, why it holds its value, what it's used for today, and how it differs from a digital pound. Calm, clear and free of hype.

discoveries.headline: COP31 opens: leaders told to 'get serious'
discoveries.why: Two minutes on how the Antalya summit began: a late start after an all-night fight over money for vulnerable countries, Guterres pushing for faster cuts, and Australia running the negotiations. Ask yourself: who pays, and who gets left out?

discoveries.headline: A teenager's dung beetle wins Young Wildlife Photographer of the Year
discoveries.why: Oscar Whitfield crouched low in Zimbabwe's Zambezi National Park to show a dung beetle at work, and it won the top young photographer's prize. Proof that the small, overlooked things are worth getting down on your knees for. Find one today.
discoveries.credit: 'Labour of Love' © Oscar Whitfield, Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026

discoveries.headline: Rest in the space of loving awareness
discoveries.why: Tara Brach's newest guided sit, out yesterday: twenty minutes to soften, widen and let whatever is here be held in kindness. Ideal for the walk or the bus with headphones on.

discoveries.headline: How selfish are we, really?
discoveries.why: Cambridge social scientist Jonathan Goodman argues we're built for both cooperation and quiet competition, and which one shows up depends on who's watching. His answer: design for fairness, and make cheating hard to hide. A great lens for any community you're building.

discoveries.headline: Omar Musa's Fierceland, this year's Miles Franklin winner
discoveries.why: Two siblings discover that Sydney and Los Angeles can't free them from their father's palm-oil legacy in Borneo. The judges called it a tour de force, with the forest itself as the moral heart. Champion it: borrow it, buy it, or tell one friend.

discoveries.headline: Eric Topol on the keys to healthy ageing
discoveries.why: One of medicine's most trusted researchers walks through what 'super agers' have in common: sleep, movement, food and a strong immune system matter more than luck, and protein mania is overdone. Evidence, not miracle claims. General information, not medical advice.
discoveries.source: Health & Veritas, Yale School of Management
discoveries.meta_credit: Health & Veritas · Yale School of Management

discoveries.headline: Heart and hips: let go, hands-free
discoveries.why: Adriene's 26-minute flow for tight shoulders and hips, and the feelings we store there. You'll want a towel, tie or strap. Slow, kind and free.

discoveries.headline: Strength training just got simpler
discoveries.why: Harvard Health on the new guidance: two days a week, every major muscle group, 2 to 3 sets of 8 to 10 reps, and no need to train to exhaustion. When it feels easy, add a little weight. That's the whole ritual.
